product: Attruby (acoramidis), a near-complete TTR stabilizer for ATTR-CM, generated $222.4M U.S. net product revenue in Q2 2026 (2026-08-10 SEC 8-K Ex-99.1). Pipeline demand drivers under FDA review: BBP-418 for LGMD2I/R9, encaleret for ADH1, oral infigratinib for achondroplasia, plus royalty from partner-sold BEYONTTRA.
demand: Volume and diagnosis led, not price. First-line treatment-naive share rose again and total market grew 19 percent quarter over quarter (51 percent year over year) with Attruby up 23 percent; gross-to-net stayed inside the guided 30-40 percent; management said it will not match Pfizer rebates, relying on clinical differentiation (2026-08-10 call). Mix has first-line strength offsetting a smaller switch pool.
pricing_power: Gross-to-net widening past 30-40 percent if Pfizer triggers a rebate or price war; Q2 2026 operating costs of $350.8M with SG&A up $57.1M year over year to fund three launches; $41.3M per quarter noncash interest on deferred royalty obligations; preferred-equity obligations; generic tafamidis in the U.S. mid-2031 pressuring ATTR-CM pricing.
competition: No near-term Chinese or generic acoramidis; it is a small molecule still brand-protected. The realistic low-cost substitute is generic tafamidis, which management expects in the United States in mid-2031 (2026-08-10 call). Eplontersen and vutrisiran are alternatives but not low-cost. No dated generic entry before 2031 found.
market_strategy: 2026-08-10 CEO Neil Kumar said he expects Attruby to keep growing first-line share and to show significant commercial fruit in the 6- to 9-month range, with over $10B risk-adjusted revenue ($8B post-Phase 3). 2026-08-31 Kumar said BridgeBio has already launched the lowest-priced product with the best data at 30 months.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $243.7M vs $110.6M y/y, Attruby $222.4M vs $71.5M, first-line share up, gross-to-net stable 30-40%, $1.7B pro forma cash, MFN deal removes pricing-mandate risk, three NDAs under review.
bear: Attruby revenue fell 10.7% since earnings; SG&A up $57.1M y/y; $41.3M/quarter noncash interest; KKR overhang; generic tafamidis mid-2031; BBP-418 and encaleret PDUFA binary risks; gross-to-net could widen past 40%.
falsifier: BBP-418 receives a CRL on or before its 2026-11-27 PDUFA date, or Q3 2026 Attruby U.S. net product revenue fails to grow above $222.4M.

web_demand_product: Attruby (acoramidis), a near-complete TTR stabilizer for ATTR-CM, generated $222.4M U.S. net product revenue in Q2 2026 (2026-08-10 SEC 8-K Ex-99.1). Pipeline demand drivers under FDA review: BBP-418 for LGMD2I/R9, encaleret for ADH1, oral infigratinib for achondroplasia, plus royalty from partner-sold BEYONTTRA.
web_price_volume_mix: Volume and diagnosis led, not price. First-line treatment-naive share rose again and total market grew 19 percent quarter over quarter (51 percent year over year) with Attruby up 23 percent; gross-to-net stayed inside the guided 30-40 percent; management said it will not match Pfizer rebates, relying on clinical differentiation (2026-08-10 call). Mix has first-line strength offsetting a smaller switch pool.
web_bottleneck: Diagnosis and patient identification, not supply. Fewer than 5 percent of rare diseases have an FDA-approved treatment (2026-09-25 X). More than 2,200 ADH patients identified under ICD-10 E20.810 at about 70 new diagnoses per month; roughly 500 genetically confirmed LGMD2I/R9 U.S. patients; ~700 target institutions and 5,300 specialists (2026-08-10 SEC 8-K Ex-99.1 and call).
web_who_benefits_next: Kidney-orphan indication expansion pulls in nephrologists; BEYONTTRA partners via $15.4M quarterly royalty; genetic-testing labs and the MDA Care Center Network for LGMD2I/R9; preferred-equity holders Sixth Street, HealthCare Royalty and KKR; contrast-imaging and RWE data vendors feeding payer and guideline arguments.
web_who_loses: Pfizer loses first-line ATTR-CM share and pricing leverage (tafamidis/Vyndamax). Alnylam (Amvuttra) and Ionis/AstraZeneca lose silencer volume; eplontersen CARDIO-TTRansform missed its primary endpoint around July 2026, weakening combination therapy. BioMarin (vosoritide) faces an oral rival in achondroplasia. Ascendis PTH faces oral encaleret in hypoparathyroidism.
web_margin_collapse_risk: Gross-to-net widening past 30-40 percent if Pfizer triggers a rebate or price war; Q2 2026 operating costs of $350.8M with SG&A up $57.1M year over year to fund three launches; $41.3M per quarter noncash interest on deferred royalty obligations; preferred-equity obligations; generic tafamidis in the U.S. mid-2031 pressuring ATTR-CM pricing.
web_low_cost_substitute: No near-term Chinese or generic acoramidis; it is a small molecule still brand-protected. The realistic low-cost substitute is generic tafamidis, which management expects in the United States in mid-2031 (2026-08-10 call). Eplontersen and vutrisiran are alternatives but not low-cost. No dated generic entry before 2031 found.
web_ceo_promised: 2026-08-10 CEO Neil Kumar said he expects Attruby to keep growing first-line share and to show significant commercial fruit in the 6- to 9-month range, with over $10B risk-adjusted revenue ($8B post-Phase 3). 2026-08-31 Kumar said BridgeBio has already launched the lowest-priced product with the best data at 30 months.
web_did_they_deliver: Largely yes on operations. 2026-08-10: Q2 revenue $243.7M versus $110.6M year over year, Attruby $222.4M versus $71.5M; all three NDAs submitted; encaleret granted Priority Review 2026-07-22; $1B preferred equity closed 2026-07-01. But the equity fell 10.7 percent since the earnings report (Yahoo 2026-09-09).
web_what_would_falsify: BBP-418 receiving a CRL on or before the 2026-11-27 PDUFA date, or Q3 2026 Attruby sequential U.S. net product revenue failing to grow above $222.4M, or gross-to-net widening beyond 40 percent, or an encaleret CRL by 2027-05-08. Any one would break the launch-and-margin thesis.
